cards.a: GNS3 is a free GUI that runs real device images (IOS, IOS-XE, and any VM) plus Docker containers, running images via QEMU and dynamips, popular for CCNP lab practice without Cisco licensing.

cards.q: Why is GNS3 popular for CCNP lab practice?
cards.a: It is free and flexible, runs real device images plus VMs and Docker, is automation-friendly, and needs no Cisco licensing.

cards.q: Which image types can GNS3 run?
cards.a: IOS via dynamips for routers, IOS-XE via QEMU for modern routers, firewalls like ASAv, Linux VMs as hosts/services, Docker containers, and VPCS for simple PCs.

cards.q: What are the components of GNS3 architecture?
cards.a: GNS3 server for compute, GNS3 GUI as the client, QEMU for virtualization, Dynamips for IOS emulation, and Docker for containers.

cards.q: What is the difference between Dynamips and QEMU in GNS3?
cards.a: Dynamips emulates IOS images, while QEMU is used to run IOS-XE and other virtual machine images.

cards.q: What is the correct order when building a GNS3 lab?
cards.a: Add the image first, then drop nodes on the canvas, connect them, boot and configure, save the project, and export/import as needed.
It exposes an API for scripts, pairs with Docker for code development, supports cloud integration as a bridge, and works with Ansible for configuration.

cards.q: Which resource factors matter most in a GNS3 lab?
cards.a: CPU and RAM per node because images are heavy, plus disk space for large images; the compute server can be local or remote.

cards.q: How does GNS3 compare to CML and EVE-NG?
cards.a: GNS3 is free, runs real images plus VMs, supports Docker, has an API and high fidelity, and uses a desktop UI — a flexible middle ground.

cards.q: What is the default GNS3 API endpoint for local access?
cards.a: The GNS3 API is available via curl at http://127.0.0.1:3080/v2/.

cards.q: A GNS3 node is stuck idle and not booting. What should you check?
cards.a: Check the emulator and image configuration, since a node stuck idle is likely caused by an image or emulator misconfiguration.

cards.q: A GNS3 node has no console access. What is the likely cause and check?
cards.a: The likely cause is a port/binding issue, so check the console port bind configuration.

cards.q: GNS3 requires a Cisco license to use IOS images.
cards.a: False — GNS3 runs real images without requiring Cisco licensing, which is one reason it is popular for CCNP practice.

cards.q: Which emulator runs IOS images and which runs IOS-XE in GNS3?
cards.a: Dynamips runs IOS images, while QEMU runs IOS-XE (modern router) images.

cards.q: What hardware should you plan for when running GNS3 images?
cards.a: Heavy CPU and RAM per image, plus disk for large image files; plan resources per node before scaling a lab.

cards.q: Which free tool is best for flexible CCNP labs combining real images, VMs, Docker, and automation?
cards.a: GNS3, which provides free, high-fidelity labs with real IOS images, VM support, Docker, and an API, without Cisco licensing.
